papers.title_en: A Decade of Learning-Based Control: From Theoretic Foundations to Practical Deployment
papers.authors: Angela P. Schoellig, Matthias A. Müller, Sebastian Trimpe, Melanie N. Zeilinger, Mahathi Anand, Andrea Carron, Oliver Hausdörfer, Victor G. Lopez, Friedrich Solowjow, Haocheng Zhao, Siqi Zhou
papers.evidence: 融合机器学习与控制理论的学习型控制综述
papers.tldr: 学习与控制交叉领域缺乏兼顾理论保证与真实部署的系统入门材料。本文以十年CDC特邀专题为基础，梳理稳定性与安全保证、学习动力学模型、强化学习/模仿学习/贝叶斯优化等策略学习方法。文章总结代表性应用与开放挑战，并提供实现示例和在线资源。该教程为可靠学习型控制的入门与实践提供统一参考。
papers.abstract_en: Motivated by ten years of Learning-Based Control Invited Sessions at the IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC), this tutorial paper reviews key advances at the intersection of machine learning and control. We focus on methods that combine the flexibility of machine learning techniques with the structure and theoretical foundations of control to design autonomous systems that are capable, reliable, and safe. We first introduce core notions for establishing stability and safety guarantees, then review approaches that learn dynamics models to improve control under uncertainty, and finally discuss data-driven methods that directly synthesize or learn policies, including reinforcement learning, imitation learning, and Bayesian optimization. We further discuss representative applications and open challenges. The goal is to provide an accessible entry point to the field and to support continued progress toward reliable learning-based control in real-world systems. To support learning and practical exploration, we share implementations and illustrative examples along with our discussion, together with additional resources on our website: https://learning-based-control.github.io/tutorial/.

papers.title_en: RoboMMT: Learning Stable Tracking of Modulated Expressive and Interactive Robot Motion
papers.evidence: 模块化运动跟踪控制架构
papers.tldr: 表达性机器人动作能提升人机交互自然度，但在动态不稳定平台上实时执行时易触及稳定边界，尤其当表达性与物理控制解耦。RoboMMT 将参数化表达动作合成、基于物理的角色控制和面向空间交互目标的反应式适应组合为模块化控制架构，并训练覆盖广泛表达域的参考条件跟踪策略。四足与两款人形实验表明，该跟踪器在整个调制域内保持稳定与准确，而无覆盖训练的策略会失稳或掉精度；闭环目标适应还能实现面向与指向交互，并完成四足重扰动下的零样本仿真到现实迁移。
papers.abstract_en: Expressive robot motion can improve naturalness, effectiveness, and perceived likability in human-robot interaction. When deployed on dynamically unstable platforms, however, reactive execution of expressive body motion may bring the robot to its stability limits, especially when expressivity is decoupled from physical control. In this paper, we present RoboMMT (Robot Modulated Motion Tracking), a modular control architecture that couples parameterized expressive motion synthesis, physics-based character control, and reactive adaptation to spatial interaction goals. Our approach trains a reference-conditioned tracking policy across a broad domain of expressivity, enabling it to faithfully realize the commanded motions while maintaining dynamic stability. Goal reactivity is achieved by training lightweight, task-specific interaction policies that modulate the reference generator's spatial goal-attraction point, with the stabilizing tracking policy kept in the loop. Evaluations on a quadruped and two humanoid robots show that the learned tracker remains stable and accurate across the entire modulation domain, whereas trackers trained without this coverage lose balance, tracking accuracy, or both. We show that layering closed-loop goal adaptation over this foundation enables interactive facing and pointing behaviors, while maintaining stable execution and comparable reference-tracking fidelity. The robot learns to proactively redistribute its weight and take corrective steps. Zero-shot sim-to-real transfer is demonstrated through real-robot experiments on a quadruped under heavy disturbances.

papers.title_en: Reinforced Iterative Learning Control for elastic joint arms: Guaranteed cross-trajectory generalization under model uncertainties
papers.authors: Yuri De Santis, Michele Pierallini, Franco Angelini, Manolo Garabini
papers.evidence: 将迭代学习控制与强化学习结合用于机器人轨迹跟踪
papers.tldr: 弹性关节机械臂轨迹跟踪受非线性和模型不确定性困扰，传统ILC对新轨迹需重复学习，RL虽可泛化却样本效率低、精度有限。本文提出RILC，将ILC与RL并发耦合：ILC提供高质量样本，RL作为跨迭代的泛化尽力策略。理论证明RL不破坏ILC稳定性，并在特定条件下渐近降低误差界。仿真与4自由度串联弹性机器人实验表明，该方法可跨轨迹快速适应并保证跟踪收敛。
papers.abstract_en: Trajectory tracking for compliant robots is challenging due to nonlinear dynamics and modeling uncertainties, often requiring learning-based methods to avoid explicit parameter identification. Iterative Learning Control (ILC) ensures theoretically high precision and preserves the passive compliance of the robot. However, traditional ILC requires a separate learning phase for each new trajectory. Conversely, Reinforcement Learning (RL) generalizes to new trajectories, but practically suffers from high sample complexity and limited tracking precision. This work proposes Reinforced Iterative Learning Control (RILC) that combines the strengths of both approaches to achieve fast adaptation and guaranteed tracking convergence across diverse trajectories. By establishing a concurrent coupling between the two controllers, RILC overcomes the high initial errors and slow adaptation of traditional ILC, enabling high-performance tracking from the very first trials. In this architecture, ILC provides high-quality samples, while RL contributes as a generalizing best-effort policy across iterations. Additionally, a theoretical proof is presented to show that the RL component preserves ILC stability and, under specific conditions, can also reduce the error bound asymptotically. The efficacy of this framework is demonstrated through simulation and experiments on an underactuated 4-degree-of-freedom serial elastic robot using different trajectories and modeling mismatches.

papers.title_en: Learning Structured Locomotion References for Optimization-Based Whole-Body Control
papers.authors: Ömer Tarık Banuş, Uluç Saranlı, M. Mert Ankaralı
papers.evidence: 强化学习与优化型全身控制的分层结合
papers.tldr: 四足机器人运动需协调身体、接触力、落足与步态。本文提出分层控制器，让强化学习调节结构化运动参考，而步态调度、反应式落足规划与全身冲量控制负责高频执行。模型基座可独立维持小跑，策略专注学习何时及如何修正。在六向扰动课程与统一评测下，平均存活率达77.29%，高于参考控制器的50.35%；消融还显示自适应落足贡献最大。
papers.abstract_en: Quadruped locomotion requires coordinating body motion,contact forces, foothold placement, and gait timing. We present a hierarchical controller in which reinforcement learning adapts these structured locomotion references while a gait scheduler, reactive footstep planner, and whole-body impulse controller retain responsibility for high-frequency execution. The model-based backbone can sustain a nominal trot independently, allowing the policy to focus on when and how to modify an already functional locomotion controller. We train the complete hierarchy in a vectorized controller-in-the-loop environment using a six-direction disturbance curriculum. Under a common simulator and evaluation protocol, the proposed controller achieves 77.29% mean survival across the tested disturbance grid, compared with 50.35% for the model-based reference controller. Training-time channel ablations identify adaptive foothold placement as the largest marginal contributor to grid survival and reveal direction-dependent effects of gait-rate adaptation. Together, these results demonstrate the viability of the proposed hierarchical controller architecture for integrating learned adaptation with optimization-based whole-body control through structured locomotion references.

papers.title_en: Towards instance-dependent regret optimality in Episodic MDPs with Posterior Sampling
papers.authors: Victor Boone, Cyrille Kone, Waris Radji, Odalric-Ambrym Maillard, Dorian Baudry
papers.evidence: MDP不确定性下基于后验采样的探索
papers.tldr: 针对有限时域分段MDP中实例依赖最优性缺乏可计算方法的问题，提出π0-PSRL：用后验样本判断是否需要探索，并在探索回合执行固定参考策略π0。该设计将探索触发条件与信息采集策略解耦，缓解标准PSRL中采样最优策略未必适合探索的缺陷。作者证明实例依赖遗憾界，刻画π0带来的对数级探索成本，并给出新的问题依赖遗憾分析与Dirichlet随机变量集中结果，朝匹配渐近下界迈进一步。
papers.abstract_en: We study regret minimization in finite-horizon episodic Markov Decision Processes (MDPs). While minimax-optimal algorithms are known, tractable approaches to instance-dependent optimality are still lacking. Motivated by this gap, we introduce $π_0$-PSRL, a variant of PSRL that uses posterior samples to decide when exploration is needed, while following a fixed reference policy $π_0$ during exploration episodes. This decouples the test for exploration, triggered when the sampled and empirical MDPs have different optimal policies, from the choice of the policy used to gather information. The resulting design addresses a limitation of standard PSRL, where the sampled optimal policy may not be the optimal choice for exploration. We prove instance-dependent regret bounds for $π_0$-PSRL, identifying the logarithmic exploration cost induced by $π_0$ and taking a step toward matching asymptotic lower bounds for episodic RL. Our proof techniques showcase a novel proof structure to derive problem-dependent regret bounds in episodic MDPs, and concentration results for Dirichlet random variables, that may be of independent interest.

papers.title_en: Dissimilarity-Based Markov Decision Processes for Stabilizing State Distributions
papers.authors: Xun Shen, Yuepeng Wang, Daniyal Sajedi-Hosseini, Akifumi Wachi, Ken Kawano, Yoshihiko Fujisawa, Mehrshad Sadria, Sébastien Gros, Katsuki Fujisawa
papers.evidence: 面向随机系统状态分布稳定的策略优化目标
papers.tldr: 强化学习通常只优化期望累计奖励，难以保证状态分布收敛或稳定。本文将策略学习建模为基于差异的马尔可夫决策过程DMDP，以当前分布与目标分布的差异为目标，并给出目标分布渐近稳定的充分条件。作者引入分布的有限维表示与策略证书，量化学习与估计误差影响，并结合PPO、SAC实现。线性系统示例与HalfCheetah速度分布调节实验验证了分布反馈和目标匹配的有效性。
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning for stochastic systems typically optimizes expected cumulative rewards, while reliable and repeatable behavior also depends on how the state distribution evolves over time. Optimizing expected return alone does not guarantee that this distribution converges to a desired target or remains stable. This paper develops a theoretical framework for learning policies that stabilize state distributions. We formulate the problem as a Dissimilarity-based Markov Decision Process (DMDP), in which the policy acts on the current state distribution and the objective measures its dissimilarity to a target distribution. We establish sufficient conditions under which the optimal policy makes the target distribution asymptotically stable. To support policy learning, we introduce a finite-dimensional representation of distributions and show how stability guarantees for its parameter dynamics extend to the underlying state distributions. We further develop certificates for the learned policies, including their deployment using estimated distribution parameters. These results quantify how learning and estimation errors affect the guarantees and identify conditions under which learned policies retain asymptotic stability. For practical implementation, we combine distribution estimates and target-dependent rewards with PPO and SAC. A computable example on a linear system illustrates the proposed theoretical certificates. Furthermore, experiments on a HalfCheetah task demonstrate the benefits of distribution feedback and explicit target matching for regulating the velocity distribution.

papers.title_en: Integrating Flow Matching and Model Predictive Control for Safe Robot Navigation
papers.authors: Philipp Holzmann, Maik Pfefferkorn, Joao Carvalho, Ali Younes, An Thai Le, Georgia Chalvatzaki, Jan Peters, Rolf Findeisen
papers.evidence: 结合流匹配规划与模型预测控制的约束感知机器人导航
papers.tldr: 基于扩散与流匹配的学习型路径规划虽能从示范生成多样轨迹，却常缺乏部署时的约束满足与避障保障。该工作将流匹配路径规划与模型预测路径跟踪控制结合，用流匹配捕获多模态路径分布，并由预测控制器在线满足状态输入约束和规避障碍。事件触发重规划把控制解反馈到后续路径生成，使机器人在含未知障碍的杂乱环境中实现无碰撞导航。仿真表明框架在复杂场景中表现稳健，为数据驱动规划与约束感知执行提供了系统化集成方案。
papers.abstract_en: Learning-based path planners based on diffusion and flow matching can generate diverse trajectories from demonstrations but typically lack mechanisms for constraint satisfaction and collision avoidance during deployment. This work proposes a framework that combines flow-matching-based path planning with model predictive path-following control to integrate data-driven path generation with real-time, constraint-aware execution. The flow-matching model captures multimodal path distributions, while the predictive controller adapts motion online to satisfy state and input constraints and avoid obstacles using updated local sensor information. An event-triggered re-planning scheme incorporates predictive control solutions into subsequent path generation, promoting collision-free navigation in environments with previously unseen obstacles. Simulation results for mobile robot navigation demonstrate robust performance across cluttered environments. The framework provides a systematic approach to combining flow matching with predictive control for adaptive, data-driven navigation.

papers.title_en: Flow-based Spectral Kernel Learning for Nonstationary Attention
papers.authors: Zi Yang, Ying Li, Alejandro Lancho, Darío C. Larese, Pablo M. Olmos, Michael Minyi Zhang
papers.evidence: 学习表达性非平稳注意力核以提升自注意力表达能力
papers.tldr: 现有核化注意力多依赖固定或平稳核，难以适应复杂 token 交互。本文提出 FSKA，将核化注意力转化为谱密度学习，并用归一化流参数化双变量谱密度以学习非平稳注意力核，同时保持线性注意力的可扩展计算。借助更强核表达能力，模型可去掉 query-key 投影并固定正交 value 投影，减少约 40%–47% 投影相关可训练参数。分类、消融与扩展性实验显示其性能具竞争力或更优，并保持良好线性注意力内存扩展。
papers.abstract_en: Kernelized attention provides a useful perspective for understanding self-attention as a similarity-based aggregation mechanism, but existing approaches often rely on fixed or stationary kernels, limiting their ability to adapt the similarity structure to complex token interactions. In this paper, we propose flow-based spectral kernel attention (FSKA), a framework for learning expressive nonstationary attention kernels. FSKA formulates kernelized attention through spectral density learning and parameterizes the resulting bivariate spectral density with normalizing flows. This design enables flexible and regularizable kernel learning while remaining compatible with scalable linear-attention computation. We further show that expressive kernel learning enables a simplified attention design with removed query--key projections and fixed orthogonal value projections, resulting in a more parameter-efficient architecture. Controlled experiments on classification, ablation, and scalability profiling show that FSKA achieves competitive or improved performance over existing attention mechanisms, while reducing projection-related trainable parameters by approximately $40\%$--$47\%$ compared with most baselines and maintaining favorable linear-attention memory scaling. Code Available: https://github.com/ziyang18/FSKA.
